pointers.sentence: Django's documentation gives the reason a `SimpleTestCase` names no database by default: its tests are not run in a transaction, so a write would affect later tests (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`).

`SimpleTestCase.databases` is an empty set and `TransactionTestCase.databases` is `{"default"}`, which `TestCase` inherits; a class may name other aliases, or give `"__all__"` for every alias (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase`).

The same aliases, mirrors apart, are where a `TransactionTestCase` loads fixtures and flushes, and all of them where a `TestCase` opens its atomic blocks (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase._databases_names`; [Emptying the tables after each test: `TransactionTestCase`](transaction-test-case.md), [A transaction around each test: `TestCase`](test-case.md)).
The frozenset it returns replaces the class's attribute (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._validate_databases`, `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._add_databases_failures`).
The frozenset it returns replaces the class's attribute (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._validate_databases`, `django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._add_databases_failures`).
The result maps each alias to whether any test that uses it sets `TransactionTestCase.serialized_rollback` (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner._get_databases`).

`DiscoverRunner.get_databases` logs the aliases no test uses at the debug level, which a runner made without a logger, as the test command makes it, prints from verbosity 2 (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.get_databases`).

`DiscoverRunner.run_tests` passes the aliases, and those to serialize, to `DiscoverRunner.setup_databases`, and the aliases to `DiscoverRunner.run_checks`, so that the database checks run for these alone, and keeps both sets on the suite for a `ParallelTestSuite`'s workers (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.run_tests`).

`dependency_ordered` takes, round after round, the groups whose dependencies are met, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured` where an alias depends on one of its own group or a round takes none (`django/test/utils.py:get_unique_databases_and_mirrors`, `django/test/utils.py:dependency_ordered`).

`dependency_ordered` takes, round after round, the groups whose dependencies are met, and raises `ImproperlyConfigured` where an alias depends on one of its own group or a round takes none (`django/test/utils.py:get_unique_databases_and_mirrors`, `django/test/utils.py:dependency_ordered`).

For each group the creation of the first alias makes the test database, and its clones for `--parallel`; the group's other aliases are pointed at it, and each mirror at the database of the alias it names; once all are made, those to serialize are serialized (`django/test/utils.py:setup_databases`).

In its `finally`, `run_tests` gives that list to `teardown_databases`, which destroys each made database's clones and then the database, or leaves them with `--keepdb`, and puts back the `"NAME"` of the alias that made it (`django/test/utils.py:teardown_databases`).

Through the test command, a misspelt alias never reaches `_validate_databases`: `get_unique_databases_and_mirrors` passes over it, the check command fails on it once the others are made (`django/core/checks/database.py:check_database_backends`), and the `finally` destroys them.

Each becomes a `_DatabaseFailure`, which keeps the method and, called, raises `DatabaseOperationForbidden` with the class's message: `SimpleTestCase._disallowed_database_msg`, or `TransactionTestCase`'s own (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._add_databases_failures`).

It lets through a connection already open, the connection without a database (`NO_DB_ALIAS`), and, a comment says, one made by hand under an alias `DATABASES` lacks (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase.ensure_connection_patch_method`).

Both are undone as class cleanups after `tearDownClass`: `SimpleTestCase._remove_databases_failures` puts each method back, and `ensure_connection` is restored (`django/test/testcases.py:SimpleTestCase._remove_databases_failures`).
Django's documentation says `skipIfDBFeature` needs all the features (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`); the code needs one.
A skipped base skips the class; otherwise the first condition that holds sets the attribute to `True`, with the reason (`django/test/testcases.py:CheckCondition.__get__`).
